lead.headline: Coldcard breach exposes $247M July hole in self-custody thesis as hardware security fails at scale
lead.tldr: July's $247 million in crypto losses—second-worst month of 2026—centers on Coldcard hardware wallet compromises that transfer custody risk from institutions to physical devices without solving for key-generation vulnerabilities. The pattern reframes how investors underwrite security infrastructure: hardware alone is not a moat.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, here is what moved in Web3 over the last 24 hours and why custody risk is being repriced across the stack.

top_signals.title: Your Keys, Not Your Coins: Coldcard Wallets Hacked for $130m and Counting
top_signals.summary: Coldcard hardware wallets have reportedly been compromised, resulting in losses of $130 million and counting. The incident highlights that removing third-party custodians transfers custody risk to the hardware and key-generation processes.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The Coldcard exploit demonstrates that self-custody hardware carries concentrated failure risk that investors have historically underwritten as 'secure by default' rather than modeling as a dynamic attack surface requiring continuous security investment.

top_signals.title: Coldcard exploit pushes July losses to $247M as second-worst month of 202614m
top_signals.summary: A security exploit affecting Coldcard has contributed to July becoming the second-worst month for losses in 2026. Total losses for the month have reached $247 million.
top_signals.why_it_matters: July's $247 million total makes it the second-worst month of 2026, confirming that exploit velocity is accelerating faster than security infrastructure spend and suggesting insurance and recovery markets remain underdeveloped relative to TVL at risk.

top_signals.title: BTCPay warns of actively exploited vulnerability that could drain funds
top_signals.summary: BTCPay has issued an urgent warning regarding an actively exploited vulnerability that could lead to the draining of user funds. Users are strongly advised to update their servers to version 2.4.2 immediately to secure their assets.
top_signals.why_it_matters: BTCPay's actively exploited vulnerability shows that even widely-deployed open-source payment infrastructure lacks the operational security cadence of mature software, creating systemic risk for merchant adoption curves that investors price into stablecoin and payment verticals.

top_signals.title: Passing the Clarity Act on digital assets is a matter of national security
top_signals.summary: The article argues that passing the Clarity Act on digital assets is essential for US national security. It warns that a lack of clear domestic regulation will drive crypto activity to foreign jurisdictions beyond the reach of American law enforcement.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The national security framing of the Clarity Act signals that US crypto regulation is being pulled toward foreign policy and enforcement priorities, which would advantage compliant domestic infrastructure players but compress margins for offshore-dependent protocols.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin tops $65,000 after 'massive surprise' US jobs miss
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin price surged past $65,000 following a significant miss in US jobs data. The payroll decline has led traders to believe the Federal Reserve is less likely to implement a rate hike in September.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Bitcoin's $65,000 surge on jobs data miss confirms that BTC is repricing as a duration asset sensitive to Fed expectations, which tightens the correlation to macro conditions and complicates the 'uncorrelated' thesis that underwrites portfolio allocation models.

deals.summary: Japanese stablecoin issuer JPYC has raised $38 million in an extended Series B funding round. The company intends to use the capital to expand its Web3 ecosystem and drive the adoption of its stablecoin.

DePIN project Vangrid has raised $9 million in a token round to develop a spatial data network designed for physical AI. The project currently utilizes a bounty system for contributors and plans to launch its native token later this year.

on_the_radar.summary: Bridge, a company owned by Stripe, has officially joined the EU MiCA register after receiving approval from Luxembourg. This move allows the firm to operate as a regulated crypto asset service provider within the European Union.

on_the_radar.title: US sanctions two more Iranian crypto exchanges under ‘Economic Fury’ campaign
on_the_radar.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department has sanctioned two additional Iranian cryptocurrency exchanges as part of its 'Economic Fury' campaign. The move follows the discovery of over $3 million in transfers between Shelbit and wallets linked to the IRGC.

on_the_radar.title: EIP-8363: Tapered Issuance Burn
on_the_radar.summary: EIP-8363 proposes a tapered issuance burn mechanism that would reduce validator rewards as the staking ratio increases. The goal is to limit issuance-driven growth and reduce dilution, though critics worry about the impact on LST-based DeFi and institutional demand.

on_the_radar.title: Crypto Biz: Crypto’s biggest business is starting to look a lot like banking
on_the_radar.summary: The article discusses the increasing convergence between the cryptocurrency business model and traditional financial infrastructure. It highlights how major players like BlackRock and Tether are integrating digital assets into institutional frameworks.

on_the_radar.title: I built Canada’s largest crypto company. But the business climate here made selling to Robinhood inevitable
on_the_radar.summary: The CEO of WonderFi explains that the company's sale to Robinhood was driven by Canada's restrictive regulatory environment. He argues that the burdensome business climate made it nearly impossible to scale the company internationally.

on_the_radar.title: 5 charts: How crypto cards are driving stablecoin spend
on_the_radar.summary: Analysis of the growth of crypto payment cards, highlighting their role in increasing stablecoin spending. The data shows a significant scale of adoption with nearly 9 million monthly purchases.

on_the_radar.title: High on Their Own Supply? Ethereum, Solana Reconsider Inflation Schedules
on_the_radar.summary: Ethereum and Solana are evaluating their inflation schedules to determine the optimal security budget required to maintain network integrity. The discussion focuses on the trade-offs between token issuance and the long-term security of their respective blockchains.

on_the_radar.title: Japan FSA asks crypto exchanges to impose withdrawal delays to fight scams26m, Japan FSA asks crypto exchanges to impose withdrawal delays to fight scamsJapanese authorities called for address registration, customer-specific limits and stronger authentication as part of a broader push to curb misuse of exchange accounts.
on_the_radar.summary: The Japan Financial Services Agency (FSA) is urging cryptocurrency exchanges to implement withdrawal delays and stricter authentication measures. These steps are intended to combat scams and prevent the misuse of exchange accounts.

worth_a_read.title: EIP-8363: Tapered Issuance Burn
worth_a_read.note: EIP-8363's tapered issuance burn mechanism deserves attention because it directly addresses Ethereum's monetary policy credibility problem that has been eroding the 'ultrasound money' narrative since the Merge.

worth_a_read.note: Galaxy's analysis of Ethereum and Solana inflation schedule reconsiderations matters because it captures the political economy of validator rewards at a moment when both chains face competitive pressure to subsidize security without diluting token holders.

linkedin_post:
Hardware wallets were supposed to be the endpoint of trust minimization. Coldcard's $130 million and counting suggests the endpoint was only a rest stop.

The exploit pattern is specific: key-generation entropy compromised, not transaction signing. That's a manufacturing and supply-chain problem dressed in cryptographic language. The self-custody thesis assumed that removing Coinbase or Celsius removed counterparty risk. It didn't. It relocated it to physical devices with firmware update cycles measured in quarters, not days.

July is now the second-worst month of 2026 at $247 million. The market is pricing this as isolated. We don't underwrite security that way. The question is whether insurance primitives, multi-sig architectures, or simply a return to qualified custodians win the repricing. Our read: the infrastructure that makes self-custody operationally feasible—real-time monitoring, secure element attestation, recovery orchestration—has been underinvested because the narrative ran ahead of the engineering.

Bitcoin at $65,000 on a jobs miss is the other side of this. Macro-sensitive, duration-like, increasingly correlated to the Fed path. Two different risk regimes. One market.

The test: if Coldcard losses hit $200 million, does self-custody hardware demand compress, or does it accelerate into 'safer' brands? We are underwriting the former.
